learning: kd 0.8 at wheel_track 0.16 is the best measured combination. Slalom remains 0 of 20 at every geometry and controller tested, so it is an open risk on the unseen track.
notes: Final package: the Builder's wheel_track 0.16 geometry with the iteration 10 controller (kd 0.8). It reproduces the best measured design (703.8) on the geometry the Builder proposed.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the package should be the most robust measured design rather than a speculative one. Iteration 10 raced the same geometry the Builder proposed (wheel_track 0.16, sensors at y 0.08, 16 mm footprints, x ±0.024 at 12 mm pitch, body 0.16 x 0.12, wheels 0.03, mass 0.8) with kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.6 and last_direction. It scored 703.8, the best in the history. Its oval finished 20 of 20 with oscillation 0.24, and its s-bend finished 20 of 20 with oscillation 0.30 and max_error 0.017. Slalom stayed 0 of 20 (line_loss 1.4, max_error 0.065), as it has at every geometry tested. Compared with kd 0.5 at the same geometry (iteration 9-era best, 661.5), kd 0.8 removed all s-bend off-track exits and cut oval control_effort from 4.6 to 2.9. I therefore keep kd 0.8 and every other controller value unchanged. The unseen final track is a different shape, so I am not adding untested changes such as kp, span or footprint. Expected result: the same behaviour as iteration 10, with the s-bend and oval as the robust core and slalom-type geometry as the open risk.
